core_ideas.core_claim: Right Click Save is a dedicated publication for long-form criticism, essays, and interviews about digital art, generative art, and NFT art. Its core proposition is that the digital art field needs serious, sustained critical writing — not just market commentary or hype — to develop the intellectual infrastructure for a mature art movement. The publication treats digital art as art worthy of the same critical attention afforded to painting, sculpture, or photography.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Entirely focused on digitally native art. Coverage spans generative art, on-chain art, AI art, NFT art, creative coding, and other born-digital practices. The publication's specificity is in treating these practices as art forms with their own aesthetic traditions, technical vocabularies, and critical questions — rather than as subcategories of 'tech' or 'crypto.' Right Click Save engages with what makes digital art distinct: code as medium, algorithmic aesthetics, blockchain provenance, generative processes, and the relationship between art and platform infrastructure.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Right Click Save operates in tension with attention economy logic. The publication produces long-form writing that resists attention-economy brevity and engagement optimization. However, it distributes primarily through social media (Twitter/X, newsletter) and depends on platform attention for readership. The publication covers artists and works that exist within attention-driven platform ecosystems (NFT markets, social media) while advocating for slower, deeper engagement. This tension is productive — the publication uses attention-economy channels to distribute anti-attention-economy content.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Strongly intention-aligned. Right Click Save serves the declared structural need for critical discourse in the digital art field. The publication exists because market commentary and hype dominated digital art coverage during the NFT boom, and the field needed serious critical writing. This is infrastructure for the field's intellectual development — building vocabulary, establishing critical frameworks, and creating historical record through published criticism.

market_economics.revenue_model: Primarily editorial sponsorships, partnerships with digital art platforms (fxhash, Art Blocks, and others have sponsored content or sections), and potentially Substack/newsletter subscriptions. The publication operates on a lean budget. Some revenue from events and collaborations. The advertising/sponsorship model creates potential conflicts of interest when sponsors are also subjects of coverage. [uncertain]
market_economics.market_position: Discourse infrastructure. Right Click Save does not participate in art sales but shapes market perception through criticism and coverage. Positive coverage in the publication can influence collector interest and artist reputation. The publication occupies a unique position as the most dedicated source of serious digital art criticism.
market_economics.price_range: Not applicable. The publication does not sell art. Content is freely accessible online.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Stable to growing in editorial output and reputation, despite the broader NFT market contraction. The publication has arguably become more important post-crash as the field seeks substantive discourse beyond market hype. Readership metrics are not publicly available. The publication has maintained consistent output through the bear market, demonstrating commitment beyond the hype cycle. [uncertain]
market_economics.collector_demographics: Not a collecting platform. Readership includes digital art collectors (crypto-native and traditional), artists, curators, gallerists, and culturally engaged technologists. The publication's audience is likely more informed and committed than average NFT market participants — people who seek long-form criticism are self-selected for deeper engagement with the field. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Fragile. The publication depends on a lean operation (primarily Sam Spike and contributing writers) and sponsorship revenue that correlates with digital art market health. If platform sponsors (fxhash, Art Blocks) face financial pressure, sponsorship revenue may decline. The publication is not backed by a major institution or endowment. Sustainability depends on continued willingness of the digital art ecosystem to fund criticism — a willingness that is not guaranteed and historically rare in any art field. [uncertain]

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Standard web publishing (website, newsletter platform, social media distribution). The publication itself uses conventional content management tools. Coverage focuses on the toolchains of the artists profiled: creative coding frameworks, blockchain platforms, generative systems, AI tools.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Critically engaged as subject matter. Right Click Save has published significant coverage of AI art, examining questions of authorship, creativity, training data ethics, and the relationship between AI-generated and human-made art. The publication has profiled AI artists and examined how AI tools are changing digital art practice. AI is covered as a medium, tool, and cultural phenomenon — with attention to both its creative potential and its disruptions. The editorial stance is generally more analytical than either boosterist or dismissive.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Published text — static artifacts (articles, essays, interviews) that accumulate as a critical archive. The publication does not produce live or interactive content. However, the subjects of coverage span all liveness modes.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Right Click Save is actively building the critical vocabulary for digital art. The publication develops language for discussing algorithmic aesthetics, generative processes, on-chain art, and the relationship between code and visual output. Contributing writers bring diverse critical frameworks — art history, media theory, philosophy, computer science. The vocabulary is more accessible than academic discourse but more rigorous than market commentary. This middle register is the publication's distinctive contribution. Key vocabulary contributions include sustained attention to what makes generative art distinct as an art form, how to evaluate algorithmic aesthetics, and how to discuss the relationship between artistic intention and algorithmic output.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Strongly openness over enclosure: freely accessible criticism, no paywall for most content. Commons over capture: the published criticism is a public good for the field. Infrastructure over spectacle: long-form writing is inherently anti-spectacle. Individual and collective: profiles individual artists but in service of building shared critical discourse.

infrastructure_governance.openness: High for outputs — articles are freely accessible online. The editorial process and business operations are not transparent. No open-source tools or data. The publication is open in its distribution but proprietary in its operation.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Founding-team. Sam Spike as editor-in-chief makes editorial decisions, likely with input from contributing writers and advisors. No formal community governance, advisory board (publicly known), or democratic editorial process. This is a founder-driven publication.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Contributing writers retain their copyright in most publication models, though specific terms are not publicly documented. The publication controls its archive and distribution. Readers have no data sovereignty concerns beyond standard web analytics. [uncertain]
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Low. Right Click Save is a conventional web publication. No APIs, structured data exports, or machine-readable formats. Articles are not tagged with standardized metadata that would enable systematic connection to other knowledge systems. The publication's knowledge is locked in article format.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Standard web hosting — articles exist on the website and can be accessed through web archives (Wayback Machine). No dedicated preservation strategy. If the publication ceases operation, its archive would depend on the founder's decisions about the domain and hosting. No institutional backup or distributed preservation. This is a significant vulnerability for a publication that serves as critical infrastructure. [uncertain]
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Absent in any formal sense. Standard publication consent (writers agree to publish, subjects agree to be interviewed). No granular or machine-readable consent framework.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Bridge. Right Click Save translates digital art for audiences familiar with art criticism (using recognizable critical frameworks) while maintaining specificity about what is digital-native. The publication's tone and format are closer to traditional art criticism (long-form essays, in-depth profiles) than to crypto/tech media. This positions it as a bridge between digital art culture and traditional art world discourse.
field_position.what_it_enables: Serious critical discourse for digital art that previously lacked it. A historical record of the field through published criticism. Vocabulary development for discussing algorithmic and generative aesthetics. Artist visibility through profiles and interviews that go deeper than market listings. A counter-narrative to market hype through analytical criticism. A reference point for curators, collectors, and institutions seeking to understand digital art.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Institutional backing that would ensure long-term survival. Geographic and cultural diversity — the publication is primarily Anglophone and Western-oriented. Peer review or editorial plurality (founder-driven publications carry the risk of singular perspective). Systematic coverage of the field (coverage is selective, not comprehensive). Connection to academic discourse (more accessible but less rigorous than academic publications). Revenue model that does not depend on the platforms and markets it covers.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Non-Anglophone digital art communities. Artists working in traditions not recognized by the publication's editorial frame (e.g., some forms of commercial digital art, game art, social media art). Practitioners in the Global South whose work is not covered. Readers who cannot engage with long-form English-language criticism. Writers from non-Western critical traditions who may not have access to the publication's network.
field_position.frontier_signal: Emerging, maturing. Right Click Save was frontier when launched during the NFT boom as the first dedicated serious criticism publication for digital/NFT art. It has matured into an established voice but remains young and fragile. The frontier question is whether specialist criticism publications can sustain themselves financially in a post-hype environment.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Social media (Twitter/X is the primary discovery channel), newsletter subscriptions, word of mouth in digital art community, links from artists and collectors sharing articles, search engine traffic, and cross-promotion with digital art platforms that sponsor content.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Moderate-high. The publication depends on social media (particularly Twitter/X) for distribution and reader acquisition. If Twitter/X disappeared, the publication would lose its primary distribution channel and would need to rebuild through newsletter and other channels. The newsletter provides a direct channel that reduces platform dependency, but initial discovery is heavily platform-dependent.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Intention-native. The publication serves the declared structural need for critical discourse. It exists to build the field's intellectual infrastructure, not to capture engagement. However, the sponsorship model creates potential tension — sponsors may prefer coverage that supports their platforms' market position. The degree to which editorial independence is maintained despite sponsorship relationships determines the actual intention alignment.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: High. Published criticism is a significant commons contribution — freely accessible writing that builds shared vocabulary, creates historical record, and develops critical frameworks for the field. Each article adds to the collective knowledge base. The publication is one of the most important commons resources for digital art criticism. The limitation is that the knowledge is in article format rather than structured, machine-readable data.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Meaning provenance. The publication tracks the cultural significance, critical context, and artistic meaning of digital art — not ownership or transaction history. Articles provide provenance of interpretation — documenting how works and artists are understood at specific historical moments.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Primarily present-focused with emerging archival quality. The publication covers current artists and works but the accumulating archive of criticism is becoming a historical resource. No systematic deep-historical or anticipatory orientation, though individual articles may look backward or forward.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Implicit rather than systematic. Editorial choices about what to cover necessarily highlight what the publication deems important, which implicitly identifies what was previously absent from critical discourse. However, there is no formal mechanism for mapping gaps in the field or identifying what is missing from coverage.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence. The publication holds together diverse perspectives through a shared commitment to serious criticism. Different contributing writers bring different critical frameworks and positions. The editorial voice provides coherence without demanding consensus on aesthetic or theoretical questions.
coherence.contestability: Low formal contestability. Readers can respond on social media but there is no formal letters-to-the-editor, peer review, or editorial challenge mechanism. The publication's interpretations and evaluations are presented as authoritative criticism, which by convention is contestable through counter-criticism rather than formal process.
coherence.forkability: High. The model (online publication with long-form digital art criticism) could be replicated by anyone with critical writing skills and editorial commitment. No proprietary technology, data, or infrastructure barriers to forking. The main barrier is the accumulated reputation and writer network, which take years to build.

adai_comparison.layer_mapping: sensing-loop (criticism as field sensing and interpretation)
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The commitment to long-form, serious criticism as field infrastructure. The middle register between academic density and market commentary. The treatment of digital art as deserving the same critical attention as any other art form. The demonstration that a lean operation can make outsized contributions to field discourse. The persistence through market cycles (continuing through the bear market when hype-driven publications folded).
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The founder-driven editorial model that concentrates critical authority. The dependence on platform sponsors who are also subjects of coverage (conflict of interest risk). The lack of structured, machine-readable knowledge outputs (criticism as articles only, not as data). The absence of institutional preservation strategy for the critical archive. The Anglophone/Western bias in coverage and perspective. The social media dependency for distribution.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Right Click Save demonstrates that dedicated criticism infrastructure can serve the digital art field, but its model is fragile, founder-dependent, and locked in conventional publication format. The productive tension for A(DAI) is between the value of human-written criticism (which Right Click Save proves is essential) and the need for structured, machine-readable knowledge (which the publication format cannot provide). A(DAI) needs both: the depth and nuance of long-form criticism AND the structured interoperability of data infrastructure. Right Click Save shows that the field will support criticism; the question is whether criticism can be connected to broader knowledge infrastructure without losing its qualitative depth.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: UK media law applies. Standard defamation and copyright considerations for a publication. No specific exposure to EU AI Act or crypto regulation unless covering those topics (which it does editorially). Advertising/sponsorship disclosure regulations may apply to sponsored content. The publication's regulatory profile is light.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Standard publication copyright. The publication likely holds copyright on published articles (or licenses from contributing writers). No open licensing or CC publication. Standard web publication IP model. [uncertain]
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in for contributors (writers agree to publish). Subjects of coverage are covered under journalistic norms (no consent required for criticism). Newsletter subscribers opt in. No data scraping or default inclusion.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Moderate. Depends on web hosting, social media (Twitter/X) for distribution, newsletter platform (likely Substack or similar) for subscriber communication, and sponsor platforms (fxhash, Art Blocks, etc.) for revenue. The loss of Twitter/X would be the most significant single-platform risk. No blockchain dependency.
ecosystem.network_effects: Moderate bridge. Right Click Save connects artists, collectors, curators, and platforms through its coverage. Being profiled in the publication creates visibility that connects practitioners to audiences. The publication functions as a network node that mediates between different parts of the digital art ecosystem. However, the network effects are limited by the publication's modest scale.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Stable and arguably strengthened. The 2022-2023 crypto crash eliminated many hype-driven digital art publications and commentators, leaving Right Click Save as one of the few dedicated criticism venues still operating. The post-crash environment favors substantive criticism over market commentary, which is exactly what the publication provides. The publication's persistence through the bear market has enhanced its credibility. However, sponsorship revenue may face pressure if platform sponsors are financially strained. [uncertain]
